subject: Usage reconciliation: Q2 unexpected compute delta and credit request
messages:
From: Claire Dunn <claire@cloudwave.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage reconciliation: Q2 unexpected compute delta and credit request

Hi Soojin,

Hope you're well — quick one from our side. During the May 25 - June 5 window we had a misconfigured nightly enrichment job that reprocessed several buckets; that resulted in a large, unexpected spike in tokens and GPU minutes that was billed on our Q2 invoice. We've attached a short CSV (CW-usage-q2-deltas.csv) that shows the delta by day and pipeline.

The net effect is ~2.1M additional input tokens and ~12k extra GPU minutes. Our procurement team is asking for a one-time credit or amortized adjustment — we understand policy is policy, but there was no intent and the activity was self-identified. Can you advise on Redwood's process for retroactive adjustments and whether a credit is possible?

We're hoping to close this before our month-end review next week; happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Claire Dunn
Head of Data Platform
Cloudwave Analytics

Attachments: CW-usage-q2-deltas.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dunn <claire@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.ai; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage reconciliation: Q2 unexpected compute delta and credit request

Hi Claire — thanks for the quick summary and for sending the CSV. Sorry to hear about the misconfig; appreciate you flagging it proactively.

I'll loop in Finance (Laura) and Billing Ops (Ben) to review the deltas and propose an approach. Our usual options are:
- one-time credit applied to the next invoice,
- amortized credit spread across the next N invoices, or
- invoice reissue if the delta is material and within the contractual remediation window.

Can you confirm the customer IDs and the earliest run IDs for the reprocessed jobs (so we can trace logs)? Also confirm whether the traffic was from the production tenant (prod:cloudwave-main) or a staging key — that will affect remediation.

I'll aim to get a concrete proposal within 3 business days. If this is time-sensitive for your month-end review, I'm available for a 20-minute sync tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Cloudwave Q2 spike - proposed settlement

Ben/Laura — FYI thread from Cloudwave (attached CSV). High-level: 2.1M tokens / ~12k GPU minutes from May 25-Jun 5, customer self-identified. Cloudwave is asking for a one-time credit.

My initial thinking: offer a split remediation that balances customer goodwill and the economics of the term:
- If usage was on prod tenant (confirmed), propose 40% credit on the overage media (GPU minutes) given they caught it early and it was a one-off;
- Alternatively, if they provide proof it was a developer/staging key misroute, we propose 0% credit but offer guidance and a tooling credit (free debug sessions + 30-day elevated alerts).

If we go with the 40% credit, we'd apply it as a one-off credit against the July invoice (and create a negative line on the July invoice). That avoids reissuing previous invoices and is straightforward for accounting.

Can you run margin impact with DW-4821 and confirm whether we have precedent for 40%? If not, Ben, please suggest a number; Laura please confirm accounting viability and GL code to use.

Thanks — I plan to respond externally with a proposal on Thurs 6/18 to meet Claire's cadence.

Cheers,
Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Cloudwave Q2 spike - proposed settlement

Thanks for the context. I pulled the deal economics for DW-4821. Quick take: gross margin cushion is there for a one-time goodwill credit, but I'd recommend structuring to protect against repeat events. Proposal:

- Credit 50% of the compute (GPU minute) overage that is clearly attributable to the reprocessed job (not to baseline traffic). That equates to roughly a $6,200 credit based on current rates.
- In exchange, we ask Cloudwave to sign a short amendment that: (a) documents the incident window, (b) requires a root-cause verification, and (c) includes a clause that future similar incidents outside of platform faults will not be eligible for credit.
- We apply the credit on the July invoice as a negative charge and include a short line item explanation. Accounting can book this to promo/credits GL code 4007.

Attaching a quick spreadsheet I prepared with the breakdown (proposed-credit-breakdown-20270618.xlsx). If legal is happy with the wording, we can have the amendment routed for signature and ask Cloudwave to countersign.

Ben
Billing Ops

Attachments: proposed-credit-breakdown-20270618.xlsx

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dunn <claire@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.ai; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage reconciliation: Q2 unexpected compute delta and credit request

Hi Claire/Markus — thanks for your patience while we reviewed this.

Summary of Redwood's proposed remediation (aimed at being fast and minimizing bookkeeping):
1) One-time credit of $6,200 applied against your July invoice for the compute overage attributable to the May 25 - Jun 5 reprocess window (see attached breakdown).
2) We will not reissue the Q2 invoice; the credit will appear as a negative line item on July's invoice.
3) We request a countersigned amendment that documents the incident details and confirms the parties' agreement that similar future incidents caused by customer-side job configuration errors will not be eligible for remedial credits. We've attached the short amendment (Signed-amendment-DW-4821-20270529.pdf is a template; we'll generate the incident-specific countersign copy once you confirm).

Next steps we need from Cloudwave:
- Confirm whether the runs were on your production tenant (prod:cloudwave-main) or a staging key (this matters for enforcement language).
- If you accept, please countersign the amendment by Tue, Jun 22 so we can apply the credit to the July billing cycle.

If you'd prefer an amortized credit instead of a one-time, let me know and we can draft an alternate schedule. Happy to join a quick call to go through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Soojin

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,

Cloudwave Analytics
